summary: On real speech the setup-time de-esser model hardly separates harsh from ordinary voices, and the realtime de-esser cuts the sibilance band by only ~0.3-0.7 dB because its auto mode compares sibilance with a running baseline of the speaker's own sibilance, which absorbs a persistent harsh resonance. Refitting the setup model alone cannot change the audio, so nothing changes here.
method: Fit-split simulated users heard through three microphones: ordinary, bright (+6 dB shelf from 4 kHz) and harsh (+8 dB resonance at 5.5-8 kHz, Q 1.5-3). Detection uses Voice Setup's own setup-time path; audio is rendered through the native de-esser with the recommended and the factory settings; sibilant frames are labelled on the uncolored clean speech.
limitations: A constant resonance is one model of harshness; occasional piercing sibilants are what the auto mode targets.
Whether a sibilant needs attenuation is partly taste; the injected excess defines it here.
Fit split only; no adoption rule was run because no candidate was proposed.
